questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Aeromagnetic survey: reduction to pole (RTP):
options: Converts the total field to vertical gradient for shallow sources
Recalculates anomalies as if measurement was at magnetic pole
Shifts anomaly peaks to the edges of the source bodies for mapping
Applies a latitude correction for the normal gradient of the field
questions.solution: RTP: removes asymmetry of magnetic anomalies. Anomalies centered over sources. Requires IGRF removal.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Division B of the Bouma sequence of a turbidite bed consists of which structure?
options: Upper structureless pelagic mudstone division E
questions.solution: Bouma B: upper parallel lamination. Upper flow regime. Graded bedding often present. Part of complete turbidite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the age range, climatic record, and fossil content of the Gondwana Supergroup of India?
options: Permian to Jurassic. Glacial (Talchir), Coal (Barakar, Raniganj), Plant fossils (Glossopteris)
Igneous intrusions and lava flows with no sedimentary or fossil record preserved anywhere at all
Volcanic piles formed entirely by submarine eruptions along a mid-ocean ridge spreading system
Marine fossils such as ammonites, belemnites and trilobites of open-shelf marine facies
questions.solution: Gondwana: rifted basins. Damodar, Son, Mahanadi, Godavari valleys. Major coal in India.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Yardang is an erosional feature carved by:
options: Downcutting by a meandering river channel
Scouring beneath a moving ice sheet
questions.solution: Yardang: streamlined ridge carved by wind. Aligned with prevailing wind. Found in arid regions with fine-grained rock.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which geophysical method offers high resolution but limited shallow depth penetration?
options: Ground penetrating radar. High resolution, shallow (<10m)
Electromagnetic sounding for deep crustal studies beyond 100 m depth
Gravity profiling to detect large density contrasts in the bedrock
Seismic refraction using hammer sources for deep oil exploration
questions.solution: GPR: electromagnetic waves. Utility detection, void mapping, archaeology.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In an S-C mylonite fabric, the acute angle between the S and C planes points toward:
options: S planes are the shear planes while C planes are the strain planes, so the two never intersect at an angle
S and C planes are always exactly parallel to each other
S (schistosity, strain) and C (shear, cisaillement) planes. Acute angle points to shear direction
C planes record strain while S planes record the shear direction
questions.solution: S-C: S = elongate grains. C = discrete shear bands. C' (extensional shear bands) also.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes a cirque and the lake that may occupy its floor?
options: Deep narrow valley that was carved by a river and later occupied by a glacier
Feature formed by wave erosion along a high-energy rocky coastline with cliffs
Landform produced by wind erosion in an arid desert region of the world where sand is abundant
Armchair-shaped depression at head of glacial valley. Tarn = lake in cirque
questions.solution: Cirque: rotational slip, frost wedging. Headwall erosion. Bergschrund crevasse.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a zoned pegmatite, the internal zones from border to core and the inward enrichment of rare elements follow what order?
options: Uniform texture and composition throughout the entire pegmatite body, with no variation in grain size or mineralogy
Absence of zonation because pegmatite crystallizes rapidly at shallow depth
Reverse zonation in which the margins are coarser than the central core region
Border (fine) → Wall (intermediate) → Intermediate (coarse) → Core (quartz core). Rare-element enrichment inward
questions.solution: Pegmatite: LCT (Li-Cs-Ta) and NYF (Nb-Y-F) families. Giant crystals up to 14m (spodumene).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A step-drawdown test, in which pumping is carried out at incrementally higher rates, is used to estimate the:
options: Determines aquifer parameters from a single constant rate of pumping
Well loss from incremental pumping rates. C·Q² term
Measures only the storage coefficient from the initial water level
Uses recovery data alone to compute the formation loss coefficient
questions.solution: Step: s = BQ + CQ². B: formation loss. CQ²: well loss. Well efficiency = BQ/(BQ+CQ²).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral's tendency to break along smooth planes related to its atomic structure is its:
questions.solution: Cleavage reflects planes of weak bonding in the crystal lattice.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the general term for a gap in the geologic record, whose types include disconformity, angular unconformity and nonconformity?
options: Gap in geologic record. Disconformity, angular unconformity, nonconformity
A continuous sequence of strata in which no time gap or break is present at all
A break in the record produced only by faulting, with no erosion ever involved
A type of sedimentary structure that records a single uninterrupted depositional event
questions.solution: Angular: tilted older rocks below horizontal younger. Nonconformity: sedimentary on igneous/metamorphic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Isostasy is the principle that the lithosphere:
options: Has uniform density everywhere, so all blocks stand at the same elevation regardless of thickness
Is rigid and fixed in place, transmitting no vertical loads to the underlying asthenosphere
Sinks indefinitely under load, with no restoring force opposing continued downward motion
Floats in buoyant equilibrium on the denser mantle
questions.solution: Thicker/lighter crust rides higher; loading (ice, sediment) depresses it, like a floating raft.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Cleavage in mica minerals is best described as which type of cleavage?
options: Cubic cleavage (three directions at right angles)
No cleavage at all, breaking with conchoidal fracture
questions.solution: Mica: one direction of perfect cleavage. Splits into sheets.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: U-series dating: ²³⁰Th/²³⁴U disequilibrium:
options: Applicable with no upper limit to the range of ages measured
Only for fresh igneous and volcanic rocks with high uranium
Any mineral phase regardless of its origin or composition
questions.solution: ²³⁴U decays to ²³⁰Th. Disequilibrium → age. ²³⁰Th/²³⁴U = 1-e^{-λt}. Isochron method.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: During strong seismic shaking, the soil liquefaction hazard is greatest in which of the following ground conditions?
options: Densely packed gravel with good drainage
Dry clay with low moisture content
Massive solid rock with few discontinuities
questions.solution: Liquefaction: saturated loose sand loses strength during shaking. High water table + loose sand + earthquake = high risk.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The formation density (FDC) logging tool derives bulk density from Compton scattering, which is then used to calculate:
options: Spontaneous potential from electrochemical effects at shale-sand contacts for permeable bed identification
Hydrogen index from neutron moderation used to estimate water filled porosity
Formation bulk density ρ_b from Compton scattering. Porosity: ϕ = (ρ_ma - ρ_b)/(ρ_ma - ρ_f)
Natural gamma emission of potassium, uranium and thorium for shale volume and clay typing
questions.solution: Density: Cs¹³⁷ source. ρ_ma: sandstone 2.65, limestone 2.71, dolomite 2.87 g/cm³.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Glacial varves consist of annual couplets made up of which two contrasting layers?
options: Alternating sand and gravel meltwater beds
Volcanic ash and air-fall tephra couplets
Wind-blown silt alternating with lake clay
questions.solution: Varves: annual glacial lake deposits. Summer: coarser meltout. Winter: fine clay settling under ice. Used for dating.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What does Walther's law state about the relationship between vertically adjacent and laterally adjacent facies?
options: Facies that overlie each other were always deposited far apart in completely different environments
The oldest facies in a vertical succession always contains the coarsest sediment at its base
Facies are recognized only by their fossil content and never by lithology or sedimentary structure
Vertically adjacent facies in a conformable succession were laterally adjacent in deposition
questions.solution: Walther: facies change vertically = lateral facies changes. Unconformities violate the law.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In deformed layered sequences, the sausage-like segmentation of competent beds known as boudinage indicates which strain condition?
options: Dextral shear across the rock mass
Strike-slip displacement along a fault plane
questions.solution: Boudinage: layer stretched and broken into sausage-shaped blocks. Indicates extension along layering. Common in metamorphic rocks.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In which texture are plagioclase laths enclosed in pyroxene, typical of dolerite?
options: Olivine crystals polkilitically enclosed within large pyroxene oikocrysts
Plagioclase laths enclosed in pyroxene. 'Fabric' of dolerite
Pyroxene prisms enclosed within laths of plagioclase in volcanic rocks
Groundmass glass enclosing phenocrysts of quartz and sanidine
questions.solution: Ophitic: common in dolerite/gabbro. Subophitic: partial enclosure. Poikilitic: small grains in large.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A clockwise versus counterclockwise P-T-t path in metamorphism distinguishes which facies series?
options: Prograde path records isobaric cooling without any accompanying burial or crustal thickening during the cycle
Retrograde path follows exactly the same P-T trajectory as the prograde path with no change in mineral assemblage
Clockwise loops record rifting-driven heating without crustal thickening and without subsequent erosion
Clockwise (thickening → erosion): Barrovian. Counterclockwise (magmatic underplating): Buchan
questions.solution: P-T-t: prograde (burial + heating), retrograde (exhumation + cooling). Zonation in porphyroblasts.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is a digital elevation model and which terrain derivatives such as slope, aspect, and hillshade are computed from it?
options: A set of contour lines drawn on the map, with elevation labels at regular intervals
A triangulated irregular network of scattered elevation points, nothing else
Isolated point spot heights spaced at regular intervals across the whole map
Raster grid of elevation. Slope, aspect, hillshade derived from DEM
questions.solution: DEM: SRTM 30m, ASTER GDEM, ALOS 30m. Used for hydrology, landslide, viewshed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In sandstone cement paragenesis, the typical order of cement precipitation from early to late is:
options: All cement types form simultaneously during shallow burial before any significant compaction of the sediment has taken place
Early (calcite, pyrite) → Mesogenetic (quartz overgrowth, illite, ankerite) → Telogenetic (kaolinite, Fe-oxides)
All cements form during deep burial late diagenesis after compaction
Cements precipitate in a random order unrelated to burial history
questions.solution: Paragenesis: diagenetic sequence. Relative timing from cross-cutting and texture.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: (U-Th)/He dating of apatite, with a helium closure temperature of about 70°C, is mainly used to study what?
options: Closure at a low temperature of about sixty to seventy degrees centigrade
He diffusion: closure temperature ~70°C. For exhumation studies
No dependence of the helium retention on temperature whatsoever at any depth
Very high closure temperature near three hundred degrees centigrade or more
questions.solution: AHe: low-T thermochronometer. (U-Th)/He age = time since cooling through ~70°C.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is incomplete melting of a source rock, where the first melt is more felsic?
options: Incomplete melting of source rock. First melt is more felsic
Melting that consumes the entire source rock leaving no residual solid
Complete melting of the source followed by fractional crystallisation
Process in which the composition of the melt is identical to the source
questions.solution: Partial melting of mantle → basaltic magma. Partial melting of crust → granitic melt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In thin section, how does biotite typically display pleochroism?
options: Weak — pale grey with no visible color change
Absent — biotite is isotropic under crossed polars
Strong — dark brown to pale yellow (brown mineral)
Red to green with strong variation in both axes
questions.solution: Biotite: strong pleochroism. One cleavage direction. 'Bird's eye' extinction.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Based on texture and composition, granite is best classified as which type of igneous rock?
options: Fine-grained clastic sedimentary rock with graded bedding and fossils
Foliated metamorphic rock formed under low-grade regional metamorphism
Fine-grained extrusive basic rock composed chiefly of pyroxene and olivine
questions.solution: Granite cools slowly at depth, producing large crystals; it is felsic and intrusive.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Ammonite suture lines evolved in complexity over time; the order from simple to advanced is:
options: Reverse order. Ammonitic (complex) sutures always precede goniatitic (simple) sutures through the stratigraphic column
No evolution. Suture complexity stays identical from the Devonian to the end of the Mesozoic
Goniatitic (simple, Devonian) -> Ceratitic (moderate, Triassic) -> Ammonitic (complex, Jurassic-Cretaceous)
Same throughout. All ammonoids carry the same suture pattern regardless of their age
questions.solution: Suture complexity increases through time. Goniatitic: simple lobes. Ceratitic: tooth-like. Ammonitic: foliate.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Cataclastic metamorphism, dominated by mechanical deformation in fault zones, produces which rock types?
options: Thermal recrystallization adjacent to a cooling magmatic intrusion
Hydrous alteration of basalt by circulating hot seawater at ridges
Impact metamorphism producing shatter cones and coesite
questions.solution: Cataclastic: crushing, grinding. Mylonite: fine-grained, foliated. Fault gouge.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which rock mass classification system was proposed by Barton?
options: Bieniawski. Q = RQD + Jn + Jr + Ja + Jw + SRF
Terzaghi. Q = RQD × Jn × Jr × Ja (four parameters)
Q = RQD/Jn + Jr/Ja with only four parameters
questions.solution: Q: 6 parameters. Rating for tunnel support. Q < 0.01 (extremely poor) to Q > 400 (extremely good).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Why does the colour of a mineral in thin section vary with crystallographic orientation?
options: Only isotropic minerals display any visible body color in thin section
Colorless appearance in every orientation for all minerals
Pleochroism — color varies with crystallographic orientation
A constant color independent of the crystal orientation
questions.solution: Pleochroism seen in biotite, hornblende, tourmaline. Property in plane-polarized light.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In an artesian well tapping a confined aquifer under pressure, water:
options: Water rises above aquifer (confined aquifer under pressure). Flowing if > ground surface
A well that always requires mechanical pumping to lift the water to the ground surface
A well completed in an unconfined aquifer lying very close to a river channel course
A shallow dug well that yields water only during the rainy season of the calendar year each time
questions.solution: Artesian: confined aquifer with potentiometric surface above ground. Flowing artesian.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Coal washing, or beneficiation, is mainly carried out in order to achieve which result?
options: Gravity separation, flotation, dense medium. Reduces ash and sulfur
Chemical treatment with acids and alkalis to dissolve all mineral impurities
Heating of the coal in a kiln to drive off moisture and volatile matter
Crushing followed by combustion to burn out the ash content completely
questions.solution: Washing: removes mineral matter (ash). Dense medium cyclone: main method. Float-and-sink test.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The section shows 30 m of overburden above a 5 m coal seam. The volumetric stripping ratio (overburden : coal thickness) is:
questions.solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 30/5 = 6 : 1.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Proximate analysis of coal provides values for which four parameters?
options: Mineral matter content determined by ashing procedures
Moisture, volatile matter, fixed carbon, ash
Ultimate analysis including carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen
Calorific value measured by bomb calorimeter only
questions.solution: Proximate: moisture, VM, FC, ash (by difference). Ultimate: C, H, O, N, S.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To extract 10 m³ of coal, 60 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
questions.solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 60/10 = 6 : 1.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 4% moisture, 30% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (4+30+15) = 51%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which statement about porosity and permeability is correct?
options: Sand has lower porosity than shale always
Clay can have high porosity but low permeability
High porosity always means high permeability
Permeability is independent of pore connectivity
questions.solution: Clay's tiny, poorly connected pores hold much water yet transmit it slowly — high porosity, low permeability.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the chemical composition of almandine, a member of the garnet group of minerals?
questions.solution: Almandine: common in schists and gneisses. Deep red to brown.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly defines a talik and its position within permafrost?
options: Lens of glacier ice preserved within a body of permafrost that forms when a glacier advances directly over the frozen ground beneath it
Layer of ground that freezes during the winter and thaws completely during the following summer in response to the seasonal cycle of temperature change
Unfrozen ground within permafrost. Open (through) or closed (isolation). Suprapermafrost, intrapermafrost, subpermafrost
Ground that remains frozen continuously throughout the entire year without ever thawing, as occurs beneath the polar ice sheets and mountain glaciers
questions.solution: Talik: groundwater flow thru permafrost. Open talik = talk connection to sub-permafrost water.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS, topology describes which spatial relationships between features, and why is it essential for network analysis?
options: Spatial relationships: connectivity, adjacency, containment. Essential for network analysis
A raster grid data structure, in which each cell of the grid stores only a single attribute value for the layer
A method for symbolising the data layers, used purely for cartographic display purposes
An optional processing step that is rarely required for carrying out GIS analysis work
questions.solution: Topology: polygon topology (left/right polygons). Network: roads, rivers. Planar enforcement.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Slope stability: factor of safety FS = resisting forces / driving forces. FS > 1:
questions.solution: FS > 1: stable. FS = 1: marginally stable. FS < 1: failure. Design: FS > 1.3-1.5.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is a pyroclastic flow deposit whose glass shards fuse at high temperature?
options: Lava flow that cools to form a dense aphanitic rock with prominent flow banding
Air-fall tephra layer that accumulates without any subsequent welding
Sedimentary deposit of reworked ash and pumice laid down in water
Pyroclastic flow deposit. Welded: glass shards fused at high temperature
questions.solution: Ignimbrite: welded pyroclastic. High temperature (>600°C) → welding. Devitrification of glass shards.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Where and around what age is the Palaeogene-Neogene boundary placed in the Indian stratigraphic record?
options: Around 23-24 Ma. Oligocene-Miocene transition. Siwalik start ~18 Ma
66 Ma, the K-Pg boundary marked by the Deccan Traps flood basalt eruption
56 Ma, the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum with deep-sea benthic extinction
34 Ma, the Eocene-Oligocene boundary with the onset of Antarctic glaciation
questions.solution: Paleogene-Neogene: Kutch and Assam basins (marine). Himalayan foreland basin (Siwalik).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Into which broad categories are continental, transitional, and marine sedimentary environments classified?
options: Only continental environments, excluding fluvial, glacial and desert systems entirely
Only marine environments, with no transitional or continental systems recognized
Continental (fluvial, aeolian, glacial), Transitional (delta, beach, lagoon), Marine (shelf, deep sea)
Only transitional environments such as deltas, beaches and lagoons, with continental and marine settings completely excluded
questions.solution: Each environment produces diagnostic sedimentary structures and facies.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Kyanite, the high-pressure polymorph of Al2SiO5 with bladed habit, is stable in which facies?
options: Low-P polymorph of Al2SiO5. Square section in contact aureoles
High-T polymorph of Al2SiO5. Needles in granulite facies rocks
High-P polymorph of Al2SiO5. Bladed. Blueschist to amphibolite facies
Mg-Al silicate with hexagonal twinning typical of low-pressure metamorphic zones
questions.solution: Kyanite: high pressure. Blue color. Hardness varies (4.5 parallel to 7 perpendicular to c-axis).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Electromagnetic (EM) geophysical methods, well suited for groundwater due to conductive overburden, operate in which two main domains?
options: Time-domain (TDEM) and frequency-domain (FDEM). Conductive overburden → good for groundwater
Measures dc resistivity with four electrodes expanded about a fixed centre point for vertical sounding
Uses the travel time of refracted seismic waves to map the depth to the top of bedrock
Probes the gravity field to identify density contrasts caused by basin fill sediments
questions.solution: EM: skin depth δ = 503√(ρ/f). Transient: airborne EM (AEM). VTEM, SkyTEM.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Carlin-type gold deposits are best described as which style of gold mineralization?
options: High-grade quartz veins filling extensional faults in granitic basement rocks
Volcanic-hosted epithermal vein systems carrying bonanza-grade silver and gold in near-surface settings
Placer deposits formed by gravity concentration in active river channels
Disseminated, sediment-hosted, arsenian pyrite. Nevada (USA). Low-grade, large-tonnage
questions.solution: Carlin: invisible gold in arsenian pyrite. Carbonate host. Sediment-hosted disseminated gold.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock retains 25% of its original parent isotope (half-life 4.47 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:
questions.solution: 25% remaining ⇒ 2 half-lives ⇒ age = 2×4.47 = 8.94 Gyr.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On the basis of hinge shape, folds are classified into which three main types?
options: Only chevron folds exist, and all other shapes are subclasses of the chevron type
All fold hinges are identical in shape regardless of the rock type or stress regime
questions.solution: Chevron: straight limbs. Box: flat top. Ptygmatic: complex, incompetent layers.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 5% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 8% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (5+25+8) = 62%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Groundwater recharge can occur through which combination of natural and artificial processes?
options: Natural (rainfall infiltration) and artificial (recharge wells, ponds, check dams)
Occurs only through the direct infiltration of seasonal rainfall into the ground surface
Results only from artificial structures built for the purpose
Happens only where sea water intrudes into the coastal aquifer
questions.solution: Recharge: ~10-20% of rainfall in alluvial areas. Artificial: managed aquifer recharge (MAR).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the approximate specific gravity of gold found in its native form?
questions.solution: Gold (Au) — SG 15-19. Heavy mineral. Placer deposits.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which option correctly describes the cross-profile of a valley produced by fluvial incision during the youthful stage?
options: Valley with a wide flat floor built of alluvial sediment
Broad valley with steep walls and a flat floor cut by ice
Fluvial incision (youthful stage). Steep sides, narrow floor
Channel pattern with multiple bars and rapidly shifting unstable channels
questions.solution: V-shaped: downcutting > lateral erosion. Rapids and waterfalls common.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which spaceborne sensor carries the MSI instrument with 13 bands, a 5-day revisit, and is suited to vegetation and agriculture?
options: The OLI sensor, with 9 spectral bands at 30m resolution and a 16-day revisit period
The MODIS sensor, with 36 spectral bands at 250-1000m for daily global coverage
The ETM+ sensor, with 8 bands, a 15m panchromatic band, and a 16-day revisit period
MSI (13 bands, 10-60m). 5-day revisit. 290km swath. Vegetation, agriculture

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What type of material is most suitable for rip-rap used in erosion protection?
options: Soft, easily weathered sandstone placed as rounded cobbles without any proper bedding layer
Silty clay compacted in layers to form a smooth impermeable face
Uniform rounded boulders of low specific gravity dumped loosely
Hard, durable rock (granite, basalt). Angular, well-graded. Weight: W₅₀ design
questions.solution: Riprap: properly sized. Bedding layer underneath. Filter layer prevents piping.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is a very coarse-grained igneous rock with crystals over 2.5 cm, enriched in rare elements?
options: Very coarse-grained igneous rock (>2.5 cm crystals). Enriched in rare elements
Fine-grained volcanic rock formed by the rapid quenching of a felsic magma at the surface
Glassy rock produced by instantaneous chilling of rhyolitic lava
Medium-grained plutonic rock with crystals between one and five mm
questions.solution: Pegmatite: high volatile content (H2O, F, Cl). Source of Li, Be, Cs, rare earths.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the stratigraphic relation, lithology, and age of the Kurnool Group in peninsular India?
options: Archean greenstone succession conformably beneath the oldest Dharwar schist belt
Overlies Cuddapah unconformably. Diamictite, limestone, quartzite. Neoproterozoic
Cretaceous marine shelf sequence with prolific hydrocarbon source rocks in the Kutch basin
Mesozoic Gondwana coal measures overlying the Archean basement in the Damodar valley
questions.solution: Kurnool: Banganapalle quartzite (diamond-bearing). Owk shale. Narji limestone.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is phosphorite, a sedimentary rock rich in phosphate minerals, defined?
options: Metamorphic rock dominated by quartz and feldspar formed at high temperature
Sedimentary rock >50% phosphate minerals (apatite). Upwelling zones
Igneous rock composed chiefly of olivine, pyroxene and calcium plagioclase
Deep-sea rock made almost entirely of biogenic silica from radiolarian tests
questions.solution: Phosphorite: marine sediments, Peru-Chile, Morocco. Phosphorus fertilizer. Guano.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Serpentinite forms by the alteration of ultramafic rocks and is notorious for which characteristic?
options: Carbonate rock formed by metamorphism of pure limestone and dolomite strata
Felsic rock composed mainly of quartz, alkali feldspar and mica minerals that shows foliation
Evaporite sequence deposited in arid restricted marine basins and coastal lagoons
Alteration of ultramafic rock (olivine→serpentine). Slip planes — landslide hazard
questions.solution: Serpentinite: tectonic melanges. Asbestos minerals (chrysotile). Weak, slippery.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) frequency affects:
options: Only horizontal resolution at the cost of depth
Depth and resolution both fixed by the antenna
Only the colour contrast of the recorded radargram
questions.solution: GPR: higher freq = better resolution but less depth. Lower freq = more depth but less resolution. 10 MHz - 2 GHz.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An ore body of 5 Mt has an average metal grade of 3%. The contained metal is about:
questions.solution: Metal = tonnage × grade = 5 Mt × 3% = 150 thousand tonnes (kt).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 30% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+30+15) = 47%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which term describes minerals having the same chemical composition but different crystal structures?
options: Two minerals having different chemical compositions and different crystal structures are polymorphs
Same composition, different crystal structure (e.g., graphite/diamond, calcite/aragonite)
Same composition and same structure forming in different habits
Same structure containing different chemical compositions
questions.solution: Polymorphs: diamond (cubic) and graphite (hexagonal) — both C.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which material property, its resistance to temperature change, is mapped remotely using day-night temperature differences?
options: Resistance to temperature change. High for wet/dense materials. Day-night ΔT for mapping
The rate of heat flow, which depends only upon the surface colour of the material that is involved
A uniform material property of the ground that is identical for all rock types present
Low for wet and dense materials such as water, while high for dry loose sand
questions.solution: Thermal inertia: √(ρ·k·C_p). Quartz: high. Water: very high. Dry sand: low. Used in geology.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Rare earth element (REE) patterns: chondrite-normalized. LREE enrichment (La/Sm)_N > 1 indicates:
options: Primitive mantle source that has undergone no prior melt extraction
Enriched mantle source or crustal contamination
Depleted source such as the mantle beneath normal mid-ocean ridges
Source in which no fractionation of rare earth elements has occurred
questions.solution: LREE enriched: OIB, arc, continental. LREE depleted: N-MORB. Chondrite normalized: divides by chondrite values.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which index minerals mark increasing metamorphic grade in pelitic rocks, and in what order do they appear?
options: A random sequence that has no systematic relation to the metamorphic grade
Chlorite → biotite → garnet → staurolite → kyanite → sillimanite (increasing grade)
Reverse order: sillimanite → kyanite → staurolite → garnet → biotite with increasing grade
An identical assemblage at every grade throughout the metamorphic terrane
questions.solution: Barrovian index minerals: each stable in specific P-T window. Increasing grade = higher T/P.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 5 km², is 3 m thick, with density 1.4 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 5×10⁶ m²×3 m×1.4 t/m³ ≈ 21 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: GPS positioning: code-phase accuracy vs carrier-phase:
options: Code and carrier-phase have identical accuracies
Carrier-phase is less accurate than code-phase
questions.solution: Carrier-phase: millimeter precision. RTK: real-time kinematic. Static: post-processed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which Precambrian rock type best exemplifies iron-rich sedimentary rocks, and what is its composition?
options: A Phanerozoic deposit of iron oxides formed mostly during the Triassic period, with chert bands absent
A sedimentary sequence rich in iron deposited mainly during the Cenozoic era
Banded Iron Formation (BIF): Precambrian, chert + iron oxides (hematite, magnetite)
Modern iron-rich muds accumulating in deep anoxic ocean basins at present
questions.solution: BIF: major Fe ore. Algoma-type (volcanic) vs Superior-type (cratonic). Banded: microbands.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Steep-sided limestone towers separated by flat plains, also known as peak clusters, characterise which karst landform assemblage?
options: Steep-sided limestone towers separated by plains. Peak cluster
Cone karst consists of conical limestone hills with sinkholes between them
Landform built up by repeated eruptions of lava, ash and other volcanic material
Landform produced by erosion of rock beneath glacier ice
questions.solution: Tower karst: Guilin (China), Ha Long Bay. Fenglin: isolated towers. Fengcong: connected peaks.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the origin and composition of deep marine siliceous rocks such as chert and radiolarite?
options: Fluvial gravels with rounded quartz pebbles and chert fragments, but with no siliceous biogenic component at all
Deep marine siliceous ooze. Radiolaria, diatoms, sponge spicules. Recrystallized to microcrystalline quartz
Deltaic sands with heavy mineral placers and abundant carbonaceous plant debris
Shallow-water carbonate sands with ooids and bioclasts, but without any silica present
questions.solution: Chert: SiO₂. Radiolarite: radiolarian tests. Bedded or nodular chert in limestone.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes a pediment at the base of a mountain front?
options: Surface built entirely of sediment deposited by rivers at the mountain front forming a wide depositional plain
Very steep cliff face cut into resistant bedrock at the mountain edge by river undercutting
Gently sloping erosional surface at mountain base. Bedrock with thin alluvium
Flat floor of a valley filled with thick alluvial sediment deposited by river flood events
questions.solution: Pediment: desert piedmont. Pediplain: coalescing pediments. Parallel retreat of slopes (Penck).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Using Mohs hardness, which comparison is correct?
questions.solution: A harder mineral scratches a softer one; quartz (7) > feldspar (6).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Stream power law: Ω = ρgQS. Incision rate E = K·Ω^m·S^n. For m=1, n=1:
questions.solution: Stream power: erosion rate depends on discharge and slope. m≈1, n≈1 (simplified.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Mohr circle for stress: center = (σ₁+σ₃)/2, radius = (σ₁-σ₃)/2. For σ₁=100MPa, σ₃=40MPa:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On a stereonet, the β-axis of a fold is determined by the intersection of which features?
options: The average of the strike directions of all measured beds on the stereonet
The pole to the axial plane plotted as a single point on the stereonet
The maximum concentration of poles to bedding contoured on the projection
Intersection of great circles through two fold limbs
questions.solution: β-axis: intersection of two great circles representing limb orientations. π-diagram: poles to limbs.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Storativity S of an aquifer is defined as the volume of water:
options: The total volume of water that an aquifer can store above the level of the water table
Volume released per unit area per unit head drop. Confined: elastic storage (~10⁻⁵-10⁻³)
The rate at which groundwater flows across a unit cross sectional area of the aquifer formation
The ratio of the saturated aquifer thickness to the hydraulic conductivity value
questions.solution: S = Ss·b (specific storage × thickness). Unconfined: S ~ S_y (specific yield, 0.1-0.3).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+35+20) = 37%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A dipping coal seam outcrops over a horizontal width of 100 m on flat ground and dips at 20°. Its true thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = horizontal width × sin(dip) = 100×sin20° ≈ 34.2 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To which structural class of silicates does the mineral muscovite belong?
questions.solution: Muscovite — white mica. Good electrical insulator. Used in capacitors.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer (K = 50 m/day) of cross-section 500 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The groundwater discharge is about:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 1 km², is 3 m thick, with density 1.4 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 1×10⁶ m²×3 m×1.4 t/m³ ≈ 4.2 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Radiometric dating works because a radioactive parent isotope decays to a daughter at a rate set by its:
options: Depth of burial below the Earth's surface
Pressure prevailing at the site of formation
questions.solution: Decay is exponential with a fixed half-life, so the parent/daughter ratio gives an absolute age.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer (K = 10 m/day) of cross-section 200 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.01. The groundwater discharge is about:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Granulite is a high-grade metamorphic rock distinguished by the presence of which mineral assemblage?
options: High-grade metamorphic. No hydrous minerals (pyroxene + feldspar + garnet)
Low-grade metamorphic rock rich in chlorite, muscovite, biotite and quartz minerals
Contact metamorphic hornfels formed adjacent to a large igneous intrusion
Mica-rich rock with a strong foliation formed at low to medium grade
questions.solution: Granulite: dry metamorphism. H2O absent. Pyroxene stable, biotite unstable.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A 3 m seam over 6 km² (density 1.4 t/m³) has a recovery factor of 0.75. The mineable reserve is about:
questions.solution: Mineable = area×thickness×density×recovery = 6M m²×3×1.4×0.75 ≈ 18.9 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is chalk composed of, and what are its characteristic physical properties?
options: Coarse-grained limestone with abundant large shelly fossils throughout
Dolomitic limestone formed by magnesium replacement of calcium
Evaporite deposit of halite and gypsum from a restricted basin
questions.solution: Chalk: White Cliffs of Dover. Pure CaCO3. Used in cement, lime.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Pencil cleavage, which yields slender pencil-shaped rock fragments in deformed rocks, develops under which condition?
options: Two cleavages intersect at high angle
A single cleavage overprints undeformed strata
Primary bedding is preserved without any strain
Shear stress rotates pre-existing fold hinges
questions.solution: Pencil cleavage: intersection of two cleavages at ~90°. Rock breaks into pencil-shaped fragments. Common in fold hinges.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 8% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (8+25+20) = 47%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquitard is a geological unit that yields little water to wells but may store and transmit water slowly; such a unit is:
options: A coarse grained unit that yields large quantities of water very easily to pumping wells
A unit that only stores water and never transmits it to wells during pumping
Low permeability unit (silt, clay, shale). Poor yield, may store/transmit slowly
A highly permeable formation such as clean gravel or heavily fractured rock of granite
questions.solution: Aquitard: retards vertical flow. Leakage through aquitard → aquitard-aquifer system.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral that effervesces (fizzes) when dilute hydrochloric acid is applied is:
questions.solution: Calcite (CaCO₃) reacts with dilute HCl, releasing CO₂ — a standard field test.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which intrusive igneous body is concordant and domes the overlying strata?
options: Concordant intrusion that domes overlying strata
Discordant intrusion that cross-cuts the enclosing country rocks
Concordant intrusion that forms broad flat layers of basaltic composition
Narrow cylindrical body filling the feeder conduit of a volcano
questions.solution: Laccolith: mushroom-shaped. Overlying beds arched upward.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Moho discontinuity, marking the base of the crust, lies at what depths beneath oceanic and continental crust?
options: 100 km. A uniform depth beneath oceans and continents, coincident with the top of the asthenosphere
2 km. The shallow depth at which the Conrad surface truncates the continental upper crust
~5-10 km (oceanic), ~30-50 km (continental). Base of crust. Seismic P-wave jump ~6.7→8.1 km/s
10 km everywhere. S-wave velocities drop sharply below this universal crustal base
questions.solution: Moho: crust-mantle boundary. Defined by Vp. Faster in mafic lower crust.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquiclude is a saturated geological unit that is essentially impermeable and yields no significant water; it is typically composed of:
options: Impermeable unit (clay, massive shale). No significant yield
A saturated permeable unit that yields useful quantities of water
A fractured rock unit with good storage and moderate transmission
A coarse sand bed that transmits water with very little resistance
questions.solution: Aquiclude: prevents flow. Confining layer in confined aquifer.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How are rock units classified and ranked in the discipline of lithostratigraphy?
options: Division of rocks based only on their structural and tectonic features
Subdivision of the rock column on the basis of measured absolute ages
Correlation of strata on the basis of their contained fossil content
Rock units based on lithology (Formation, Member, Group)
questions.solution: Formation: mappable unit. Member: subdivision. Group: several formations.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Unconformity-related uranium deposits, like those in the Athabasca Basin, are characterized by what features?
options: Placer accumulation of heavy radioactive minerals in mature beach sands
Sandstone-hosted roll-front uranium precipitated along redox boundaries between oxidized and reduced aquifer zones
Volcanic-hosted uranium associated with peralkaline rhyolite calderas
Athabasca Basin (Canada). High grade (>1% U₃O₈). Basement + sandstone. U/Pb age ~1.5 Ga
questions.solution: Unconformity: massive U within altered basement. Cigar Lake, McArthur River.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the relative duration of the Precambrian, Paleozoic, Mesozoic, and Cenozoic in the geological time scale?
options: All eras are of equal duration across the entire geological time scale of the Earth history
Precambrian is the shortest interval, covering less than 10% of Earth's recorded geological history
Precambrian (88%), Paleozoic (545-251 Ma), Mesozoic (251-66 Ma), Cenozoic (66 Ma-present)
Cenozoic is the longest era, spanning nearly half of the total Earth history span recorded
questions.solution: Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic (Precambrian). Phanerozoic: Paleo-Meso-Cenozoic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The magnetotelluric (MT) method uses what natural source field, and which parameter is measured from it?
options: Controlled dc current injected to map resistivity at shallow depth
Seismic waves generated by an airgun source to image deep crustal reflectors
Gravity measurements reduced for terrain to model the Moho depth beneath a basin
Natural EM field (lightning, solar wind). Measures impedance Z = E/H
questions.solution: MT: deep crustal imaging. Low frequency → deep. Resistivity model. MTZ: mid-crustal conductor.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On the Mohs scale of mineral hardness, what hardness value does the mineral corundum have?
questions.solution: Corundum (Al2O3) — 9. Sapphire and ruby are gem varieties.
